events.text: A refugee column comes down the western road, carts piled with bedding and grandmothers. The Demon Cult burned their valley four nights ago. The last cart has a broken wheel, and the column is leaving it behind.

choices.text: Fix the wheel and walk with them to the next town

effects.log: You carry the axle on your back for two miles. The grandmother in the cart tells you the whole history of the valley. You will remember it when the Cult is gone.

choices.text: Ask what they saw of the Cult's army

ok.log: Banners, numbers, which way they turned. You sell the knowledge to the orthodox scouts for a good price and a better name.

fail.log: Fear makes everything bigger. You come away with ten thousand demons and a dragon. It is not useful.

events.text: The orthodox sects post a call in every town square: volunteers wanted for the western passes. Food, a sword, a name in the roll of heroes, and a good chance of never coming back.

choices.text: Sign. Somebody has to

ok.log: Three weeks in the passes. You hold a bridge with eleven others for a night and a day, and when the Cult pulls back, your name is on the roll in red.

fail.deathCause: the Demon Cult in the western passes
fail.log: The Cult comes through the pass like a flood. You get out, somehow, carrying a stranger. Your name is on the roll anyway.

choices.text: Donate silver for the volunteers' food

effects.log: An army marches on its stomach. Yours marches a little further.

choices.text: Stay home. This is not your war

effects.log: You stay home. The war comes nowhere near you. You still listen for it at night.

events.text: A young demonic cultist, wounded, crawls into your woodshed to die. Fifteen at most. The black robe is too big for them. Outside, the orthodox patrol is searching every house.

choices.text: Hide them until the patrol is gone

ok.log: You lie to the patrol with a straight face. Later the young cultist leaves before dawn, and a year later a letter comes from the south: I went home. I am a farmer. Thank you.

fail.log: The patrol finds the cultist, and you. The child is taken. You are fined and remembered. You would do it again.

choices.text: Hand them over to the patrol

effects.log: The patrol thanks you. The young cultist does not look at you as they are dragged away. It is war, everyone says. You agree, mostly.

events.text: Black lanterns hang overnight on every crossroads in the county: the Cult's mark. Whoever hung them walked past the watch without being seen. The townsfolk will not go out after dark.

choices.text: Stand watch at the crossroads tonight

ok.log: At the third hour a figure comes with a ladder and a lantern. It does not leave with either. In the morning the town brings you breakfast.

fail.log: Two of them, not one. You drive them off at a cost. The lanterns go up anyway, but fewer.

choices.text: Take the lanterns down in daylight and burn them in the square

effects.log: A small, stubborn bonfire. Half the town comes to watch. It is the first time they have laughed all week.

events.text: A traveller in plain robes asks for a cup of water at your door. His eyes are red at the rims. He thanks you very politely, and asks, almost idly, whether you have ever thought the orthodox might be wrong about everything.

choices.text: Answer honestly, and send him on his way

effects.log: You talk for an hour on the step. He is clever and sad and very dangerous. When he goes, he bows to you as if you had passed something.

choices.text: Ask him to teach you what the Cult knows

ok.log: He teaches you one breathing method, in the doorway, for nothing. It works horribly well. You never see him again, and you never use it in front of anyone.

fail.log: He tries. It goes wrong inside you. He looks almost sorry as he leaves.

events.text: The road past your town is full of sect banners going to the Alliance hall: Shaolin monks, Wudang swordsmen, Mount Hua's plum blossoms, all of them making very sure not to walk next to each other.

choices.text: Follow them and watch the opening ceremony

effects.log: You watch from a tree with half the town's children. Every great master of the age, in one courtyard, pretending to like each other. It is the best show you have ever seen.

choices.text: Sell tea along the road

effects.log: Monks drink a lot of tea. Swordsmen tip better. You end the week with a full purse and a lot of gossip.

events.text: At the Alliance, an open challenge: any martial artist under forty may test themself against a disciple of the great sects, in front of every sect head in the land.

choices.text: Step into the ring

ok.log: You win. Not by much. But fifteen sect heads look up from their wine at the same moment, and at least three of them write your name down.

fail.log: You lose to a Wudang disciple with a very straight back. The Wudang elder nods to you afterwards. That is worth more than you think.

choices.text: Watch, and memorise every style

effects.log: Twelve schools in one day. You go home with your head full and spend a month trying everything on the woodpile.

events.text: An old grudge is aired at the Alliance: two sects accuse each other of the same massacre, twenty years ago. The hall is silent. Somebody needs a witness who remembers, and you happen to have been in that county as a child.

choices.text: Tell the truth, whoever it hurts

ok.log: Your story fits nobody's version, which is how everyone knows it is true. The real culprit, a third sect, leaves the hall that night.

fail.log: Nobody believes a nobody. But you told it, and one old sect head stops you on the way out and thanks you.

choices.text: Stay quiet. Great sects eat small witnesses

effects.log: You keep your head down. The grudge goes on. You sleep fine, and also not quite fine.

events.text: Late at night at the Alliance lodgings, a famous young master from a great family knocks on your door, drunk, and asks if you will be his sworn sibling. He says he likes your face. Tomorrow he will not remember.

choices.text: Swear it. Tomorrow he can decide if he meant it

effects.log: He remembers. He means it. He comes to your door at dawn, hungover and embarrassed, and you are sworn siblings for life.

choices.text: Put him to bed and leave water by it

effects.log: In the morning he finds the water and a note in your hand. Years later he sends a gift to your door at the new year. You never know quite why.

events.text: The Alliance announces its new list of heroes of the generation. Your name is not on it. A boy you once beat in a village tournament is. He sees you in the crowd and waves, cheerfully.

choices.text: Wave back and go and train

effects.log: The next list is in ten years. You have ten years. You use every one of them.

choices.text: Challenge him, here and now

ok.log: You beat him again, in front of the Alliance. The list is not changed. Everyone who matters is quietly writing it in themselves.

fail.log: He has got better. A lot better. You shake hands. Fair is fair.

events.text: The fever reaches your town. Shutters close. The physician is working three days without sleep, and the queue outside his door reaches the river.

choices.text: Help the physician: boil water, carry patients, bury the dead

ok.log: A week of the worst work there is. You learn more medicine than in any book. The queue gets shorter. The physician starts calling you colleague.

fail.log: You catch it. Three days of burning. You live, because the physician you helped sits up with you. Fair trade.

choices.text: Lock your door and wait it out

effects.log: You wait it out. You are fine. The town is not. Afterwards, walking past the new graves, you are not sure you are fine.

events.text: A merchant has cornered the market in fever-root and is selling it at fifty times the price. People are selling their houses for one dose.

choices.text: Break into his warehouse and give it away

ok.log: One night, forty sacks, every door in the poor quarter. The merchant screams for the magistrate. The magistrate, whose mother got a sack, is very busy that week.

fail.log: You get eight sacks out before they catch you. Eight sacks is a lot of lives. Prison is a small price.

choices.text: Shame him in the square until he lowers the price

ok.log: You stand on a barrel and tell everyone what he paid for the root. By noon a mob has offered to help him reconsider. He reconsiders.

fail.log: He hires two thugs and you leave the barrel faster than you climbed it.

events.text: A child at the roadside, fever-hot, with nobody. The roads are closed by order; nobody is to carry the sick between towns. The nearest physician is in the next town.

choices.text: Carry the child there anyway, by the back paths

ok.log: Through the fields at night with the child on your back. The physician takes one look and gets to work. The child lives. You never learn the name.

fail.log: The patrol catches you at the bridge. They let you through anyway when they see the child. You catch a mild fever. Worth it.

choices.text: Stay with the child and nurse them yourself

ok.log: Cold cloths, broth, three nights. On the fourth morning the child asks for dumplings. You laugh until you cry.

fail.log: You do everything right. It is not enough. You bury the child under a tree and stay there a long time.

events.text: A wandering herbalist claims he has a cure: a tea of rare mountain flowers, very expensive, in very small bags. People are queuing. Some of them are getting better. Some of them would have got better anyway.

choices.text: Test his tea yourself

ok.log: Half of it is flowers. Half of it is fever-root, real and good. He is a cheat who happens to be right. You make him halve the price, and he does.

fail.log: You buy a bag and cannot tell. Nor can anyone. The plague goes on.

choices.text: Run him out of town

effects.log: He goes. The tea was half-good, it turns out later. You never quite forgive yourself for being sure.

events.text: The fever breaks. The roads open. The town holds a festival for the living, and reads out the names of the dead at sunset, and there are a lot of names.

choices.text: Stand and listen to every name

effects.log: Two hours of names in the dusk. When it is over nobody speaks for a while. Then someone starts a song, and everyone sings.

choices.text: Light lanterns on the river for the ones you knew

effects.log: Your lanterns drift down with a hundred others. A child next to you asks who yours are for. You tell her.

events.text: The best harvest in thirty years. Every barn is full, every cellar is full, and the village has decided to hold a wrestling contest for a whole roast pig.

choices.text: Enter, and win the pig

ok.log: You throw the blacksmith's son, the miller and the miller's wife. The pig is magnificent. You share it with the whole village and become, for a week, a hero.

fail.log: The miller's wife throws you into the duck pond. Everyone agrees it is the best moment of the festival.

choices.text: Help bring in the last of the harvest instead

effects.log: Three days in the fields with everybody. Your back hurts, your purse is heavier, and you have never slept so well.

events.text: With the granaries full, even the bandits have gone soft. A notorious bandit chief comes down from the hills to the market, buys three jars of wine, and asks if anyone wants to play chess.

choices.text: Play chess with the bandit chief

ok.log: You win. He laughs, pays up, and tells you which roads his men will leave alone for a year. It is the most useful game you ever play.

fail.log: He wins three games running. He is a very good chess player. You suspect he was something else before he was a bandit.

choices.text: Arrest him. He is still a bandit

ok.log: He is drunk and outnumbered and surprisingly gracious about it. The magistrate gives you a reward. The village thinks you have no sense of occasion.

fail.log: He is drunk, not stupid. He leaves you in the duck pond, which is starting to feel like your home.

events.text: The landlord wants double rent this year, since the harvest is double. The farmers are gathering in the square with rakes and a lot of feelings.

choices.text: Speak for the farmers to the landlord

ok.log: You talk him down to the old rent and a feast for the village. He hates it. The village never forgets it.

fail.log: He will not move. The farmers pay. Next year, quietly, half of them leave for the coast.

choices.text: Pay the difference for the poorest families

effects.log: You cannot pay everyone's. You pay the widows' and the orphans'. They find out anyway. Somebody leaves a basket of eggs at your door every week for a year.

events.text: The harvest bonfire, the last night of the threshing: the whole village round a fire the height of a house, wine going round, and someone has asked you to show a sword form in the firelight.

choices.text: Show the most beautiful form you know

ok.log: In the firelight, slow and clean, sparks following the blade. When you finish, nobody claps for a long moment. Then everybody does. An old woman says she will remember it on her deathbed.

fail.log: You trip over a sheaf of rice. It is, the children agree, the best sword form they have ever seen.

choices.text: Show them a funny one instead

effects.log: The Drunken Monk, with an empty gourd. The village laughs until it cries. You do not fall over until the very end, on purpose.

events.text: With grain cheap for once, the old monastery on the hill is taking in every hungry child from three counties, and has run out of room.

choices.text: Help them build a new dormitory

effects.log: Two weeks of carrying beams. Forty children have a roof by winter. One of them follows you around for days asking how to hold a sword.

choices.text: Teach the children something useful

effects.log: Letters, numbers and how to fall without breaking a wrist. They are terrible at all three and love you for it.

events.text: A drunk in the inn sells you a treasure map for five taels: the vault of the Nine Coffin Sect, very secret, very real, he swears on his mother. You are the ninth person this week he has sold the only copy to.

choices.text: Follow the map anyway

ok.log: It is wrong about the vault and right about the hill. Under a fallen shrine, where nobody else bothered to dig, there is a box of old silver.

fail.log: You dig a very large hole in the wrong mountain, next to eight other people digging very large holes.

choices.text: Buy the drunk a drink and ask where he really got it

ok.log: He drew it himself, from memory, after a night in a tomb thirty years ago. The real map is in his head. He tells you half of it before he falls asleep.

fail.log: He drinks your wine, and sells you a second map.

events.text: Three hundred treasure hunters, all digging on the same mountain, and one of them has just found something: a stone door in the cliff. Every other digger is running towards it with a shovel and murder in their eyes.

choices.text: Get there first

ok.log: You are inside before the crowd. It is an old cave of cultivation, with one scroll of a forgotten breathing method on the wall. You memorise it and leave by the back.

fail.log: The crowd gets there first. The door is empty. There is a fight anyway. You lose a tooth.

choices.text: Stay back and treat the wounded

effects.log: By sunset there are forty injured treasure hunters and one of you. They pay in silver and stories. You come out richer than anyone who opened the door.

events.text: Your neighbour, a meek old scholar, has been digging in his garden every night since the maps started. Tonight he knocks on your door shaking, holding a muddy jade seal with a sect mark on it.

choices.text: Help him find out what it is

ok.log: It is the seal of a sect wiped out a century ago, and the old scholar is its last descendant. He weeps, and then insists on teaching you the three moves his grandfather taught him.

fail.log: Neither of you can read it. He keeps it on his mantelpiece and polishes it every morning.

choices.text: Tell him to hide it and tell nobody

effects.log: Wise advice. Within a week someone tears his garden apart looking for more. They find turnips.

events.text: Someone is selling maps to the maps now. A boy in the market offers you a map showing where all the good treasure maps are being sold. It is very cheap. He is very convincing.

choices.text: Buy it, out of admiration

effects.log: It leads to his uncle's stall. His uncle sells you a map. You end up having a very good dinner with them both.

choices.text: Hire the boy as a scout

effects.log: He knows every rumour in the county within the hour. Best twenty taels you ever spend.

choices.text: Ask him how the trick works, for free

effects.log: He explains it all, very proudly, in exchange for being called a genius. He is, a bit.

events.text: The fever dies down as fast as it came. Somebody finally found the real vault, and it was empty: looted three hundred years ago. All that was left was a note on the wall, in very old characters.

choices.text: Go and read the note yourself

effects.log: "The treasure was the road." Somebody has carved a rude word underneath. You laugh all the way home.

choices.text: Buy all the leftover shovels cheap

effects.log: You sell them to the farmers in spring at a profit. Some treasure maps pay out in shovels.

events.text: The Embroidered Guard rides into town in their silk and their silence, and posts the edict: every sword must be registered by sunset, or confiscated. The queue at the magistrate's office is very long and very nervous.

choices.text: Register your weapons like a good subject

effects.log: You give your name, your sword's name and five taels. The clerk writes slowly. Somewhere in the capital, your name is in a ledger now.

choices.text: Hide your sword in the rafters

ok.log: They search the house. They do not look up. Guards never look up.

fail.log: They look up. The fine is heavy and the guard's smile is worse.

events.text: A Guard captain stops you in the street and asks, very politely, what sect you belong to and what you know of the unorthodox gangs in the river quarter. His hand rests on his sword the whole time.

choices.text: Tell him nothing, politely

ok.log: You bore him into leaving. It is an art. He moves on to someone more nervous.

fail.log: He does not like polite nothing. You spend a night in the cells for your manners.

choices.text: Tell him what you know about the gangs

effects.log: He pays well. The river quarter finds out, as it always does. You start using a different road home.

events.text: The Guard have arrested an old swordmaster for owning a blade without papers. He has taught the village children for forty years. They are taking him to the capital in a cage cart.

choices.text: Break him out on the mountain road

ok.log: Four Guards, one ambush, one very surprised old man. He disappears into the south with your cloak. You become, briefly, a wanted name.

fail.log: The Embroidered Guard are better than their silk suggests. You end up in the cart beside him. He apologises to you the whole way.

choices.text: Petition the magistrate with the whole village

ok.log: Two hundred thumbprints on one petition. The magistrate, who was once one of the old man's pupils, signs his release with a flourish.

fail.log: The petition fails. But the cart is delayed a week, and in that week the old man's papers turn up, somehow, with a very fresh seal.

events.text: With the gangs gone to ground, the river quarter is suddenly peaceful. Too peaceful: shopkeepers are being robbed by the Guard themselves, who call it a sword tax.

choices.text: Catch a Guard robbing a noodle stall

ok.log: You trip him into the noodle pot in front of the whole market. Nobody saw a thing, officially. The noodle stall gives you free noodles for life.

fail.log: He is faster than he looks. So is his friend.

choices.text: Write to the capital about it

ok.log: Your letter reaches a censor who hates the Guard captain. Within a month the captain is posted somewhere very cold.

fail.log: The letter is never answered. You did not really expect it to be.

events.text: The crackdown ends as suddenly as it began, with a new edict and a lot of very relieved people. The confiscated swords are to be auctioned. One of them, the clerk says, is very old and very good.

choices.text: Bid for the old blade

effects.log: Nobody else knows what it is. You do, the moment you hold it. You carry it home wrapped in a blanket like a baby.

choices.text: Buy back the village children's practice swords and return them

effects.log: Fifty wooden swords, returned at the village gate. You have never been thanked by so many small people at once.

choices.text: Carve the children new wooden swords yourself

effects.log: A week of whittling by the fire. The swords are lumpy and the children adore them. The auction can keep its old blades.

events.text: A pillar of light over the Kunlun range, visible from three provinces. A secret realm has opened, the first in sixty years, and every young cultivator in the murim is already on the road.

choices.text: Go. A chance like this comes once a lifetime

ok.log: Inside, time moves differently. You find a pool of spirit water no one else noticed and come out a week later with your meridians glowing.

fail.log: The realm is full of beasts and worse people. You come out with a scar, a little energy, and a lot of respect for the word "secret".

choices.text: Sell supplies to the people going in

effects.log: Rope, rice, rumours. Everybody buys everything. You make a fortune and keep all your limbs.

events.text: Inside the secret realm, a stele carved with a method no living sect knows. Three other cultivators reached it at the same time as you. Everyone is very still, measuring everyone else.

choices.text: Fight for the right to study it

ok.log: You win the stele. You study it for a day and a night while the others wait for their turn. It is worth every bruise.

fail.deathCause: a rival cultivator in the secret realm
fail.log: You lose. You are allowed to look at it last, for a minute, through a black eye.

choices.text: Propose you all study it together

ok.log: Four strangers sitting side by side in front of an ancient stele, arguing about the third line. You leave as friends, which in a secret realm is rarer than treasure.

fail.log: Nobody trusts anybody. The stele is shattered in the fight. Nobody gets it.

events.text: Deep in the secret realm: a cultivator who went in sixty years ago, the last time it opened, still sitting in meditation by a frozen lake. Alive, barely. He opens one eye. "Is it over?" he asks. "The war?"

choices.text: Carry him out

ok.log: He weighs nothing. Outside, he looks at the sky for a long time, and weeps, and teaches you everything he learned in sixty years by the lake.

fail.log: He dies on your back at the gate, smiling, in the light. You bury him facing the mountains.

choices.text: Sit and listen to him first

effects.log: He talks for a day. Sixty years of meditation, in one long rush, most of it nonsense and some of it the best thing you have ever heard.

events.text: The secret realm is closing. The light over Kunlun is fading, and inside, everyone is running for the exit. Behind you, a young disciple of a rival sect has twisted an ankle on the ice.

choices.text: Go back for them

ok.log: You make the exit with the disciple on your back and the gate closing on your heel. Their sect sends a formal letter of thanks, and a pill.

fail.log: You make it. Barely. Half your eyebrows did not. The disciple swears a debt to you.

choices.text: Keep running. Everyone for themselves

effects.log: You make it out easily. You do not look back. You hear later they made it too, no thanks to you, and you are glad, and ashamed.

events.text: Every teahouse in the province is full of secret realm stories: dragons, immortals, a pool that turns water to wine. Most of them are lies. One old storyteller tells one that is exactly what you saw.

choices.text: Buy him tea and compare notes

effects.log: He went in sixty years ago, the last time. You are the first person in sixty years to believe him. He cries into his tea.

choices.text: Add your own story to the teahouse

ok.log: You tell it well. By next week it has a dragon in it. By next year you are the dragon.

fail.log: Nobody believes the true parts. Everybody believes the parts you made up.

events.text: A matchmaker knocks with a scroll of names and a very determined expression. Your family has invited her. She has already decided you need a match, and that she has the perfect one.

choices.text: Let her try

ok.log: The perfect one turns out to be funny and sharp and as annoyed by the matchmaker as you are. You spend the whole meeting laughing at her together.

fail.log: The perfect one is perfectly dull. You are perfectly polite. The matchmaker is perfectly undeterred.

choices.text: Hide on the roof until she leaves

effects.log: She waits four hours. You wait five. Your family is furious. It is, you agree with yourself, a martial victory.

events.text: A great family is holding a banquet to choose a match for their heir, and has invited every eligible young martial artist in the province. There will be poetry, archery and a duel. There will certainly be a duel.

choices.text: Compete in the duel

ok.log: You win the duel. The heir is watching you very closely, and not because of your footwork.

fail.log: You lose the duel but fall very gracefully. The heir sends you a note. It says: "Nice fall."

choices.text: Win the poetry contest instead

ok.log: Four lines about the moon and a sword. The whole hall goes quiet. The heir asks for a copy, in your own hand.

fail.log: Your poem rhymes "sword" with "sword". It is remembered for years, for the wrong reasons.

events.text: Your closest friend has been matched with someone they have never met, and is quietly panicking. They ask you to come and look at the person first, in secret, from behind a screen.

choices.text: Spy for them

ok.log: You report: kind, nervous, terrible at chess, laughs at their own jokes. Your friend relaxes. The match is a good one. You give a speech at the wedding.

fail.log: You fall through the screen. The match is introduced to you before your friend. Everyone handles it very well, considering.

choices.text: Tell them to go and look for themself

effects.log: They do. They come back pink. You do not ask.

events.text: Somebody has sent you a love letter, unsigned, in beautiful brushwork, with a pressed plum blossom inside. The season of matches makes everyone brave, apparently.

choices.text: Find out who sent it

ok.log: The brushwork gives them away: the quiet one who sits at the back of the teahouse. You go and sit at the back of the teahouse. You do not say anything. You do not need to.

fail.log: You never find out. You keep the blossom anyway, pressed in a book, for the rest of your life.

choices.text: Write an unsigned reply and leave it at the teahouse

effects.log: Someone takes it. The next week, there is another letter. This goes on for a whole season.

events.text: The season ends with a mass wedding at the temple: eleven couples, one priest, and a great deal of rice wine. The village has asked you to keep order, which is a joke, because nobody can.

choices.text: Keep order, badly, and dance at the end

effects.log: You break up two fights, one of them between grandmothers, and dance with all eleven couples. You go home at dawn with flowers in your hair and no memory of why.

choices.text: Stand at the gate and keep the bandits out

ok.log: Two bandits try. Two bandits regret it. Nobody inside even notices, which is how you know you did it right.

fail.log: One gets past you and steals a cake. Nobody minds. It was not a very good cake.
